reviews.decision_reason: demand_selection treats scored corpus rows as demand-bearing evidence using only demand_score >= 3 plus fallback record ids. The supplied package does not show observed customer jobs, pain, triggers, alternatives, consequences, or outcomes supporting the selected market-demand claims, so selecting all eight rows is behaviorally significant under the strict demand criteria.

evidence_normalization preserves the upstream selected rows and applies an allowed-id and bounded-window filter, but it cannot repair the missing market-demand substantiation introduced upstream. No independent defect is visible in the normalization logic itself from the supplied package.

provenance_assembly deterministically ranks normalized rows by demand_score and record_id and assembles the evidence_sources handoff, but because the normalized input already lacks strict demand substantiation, its ranks should not be treated as corroborated market-demand evidence. No separate local assembly defect is visible.
